computational_details.simulation_method: 3D cellular automaton (CA) with inhomogeneous dislocation density and grain boundary sliding

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Simulated 3D CA final AGS 65.87 µm and DRX fraction 49.59% vs experimental side-section AGS 61.38 ± 7.41 µm and DRX fraction 42.8% at 0.9 strain; simulated flow stress plateaus while experimental curve upwarps in the final segment
constant-condition flow stress accuracy RMSE 4.8944 MPa, R² 0.9909, AARE 3.91%

analytical_models.model_name: modified constitutive model (WH, DRV and DRX)
analytical_models.equation_role: describes flow stress evolution and DRX fraction kinetics under constant and varying deformation conditions
analytical_models.model_note: Material parameters are material-level constants calibrated via GA optimization and applied to this sample's 850 °C, 1 s^-1 condition

unmapped_findings: At 850 °C and 1 s^-1, the reconstructed EBSD side-section prior austenite grain size at 0.9 strain was 61.38 ± 7.41 µm with a DRX fraction of 42.8%; the 2D(YZ surface) reconstruction gave 59.08 µm and 38.7% DRX (figure_012, b0197).
The 3D CA simulation at 850 °C and 1 s^-1 gave a final average grain size of 65.87 µm and a DRX fraction of 49.59% at 0.9 strain (figure_012).
At 850 °C and 1 s^-1, the DRX-fraction vs time curve rises to about 0.4 near 1 s and does not reach 1.0, indicating incomplete recrystallization at this low temperature (figure_006).
At 1 s^-1, DRX grains experienced greater difficulty in nucleation and growth than at 0.01 s^-1 because of the increasing critical dislocation density ρc and decreasing deformation time (b0196).

The 850 °C, 1 s^-1 experimental flow-stress curve upwarps above the simulated 3D CA plateau in the final segment, attributed to interfacial friction and increased work hardening at the high strain rate (b0196, figure_011).
